notesForNextSession:
T-0296 (landing hero: one command, restored stat tiles) is in REVIEW on feat/hero-one-command, frontend-only - no API change, nothing to coordinate with the backend. The design concept put the two figures on a hairline plinth at the hero's bottom edge; that was built, then reverted to the old stat-tile treatment at the user's request. Only the PLACEMENT survives from the concept - the figures sit below the command, not between it and the copy it acts on. Three browser passes are still PENDING: a real click-through on the members figure (it resolves to href=/roster in the DOM but SPA nav was never exercised), and two that need an admin session - overlay density 0/100 against the NEW radial vignette (the stops were re-derived, so the old density verification does not carry over) and a regiment with statistics visibility OFF, where the whole block including its divider rule must vanish. Two things worth not relitigating: (1) the seam layer (.hero-overlay) is deliberately only HALF parameterised on --hero-scrim - its top stop follows the density but its fade to --ink-900 does not, because that fade is what joins the hero to the content band and dropping it at density 0 trades a bare photograph for a hard horizontal seam; (2) .hero-stat uses flex:1 1 0 equal columns rather than shrink-to-fit, because '11 / 2023' is three times the width of '2' and a centred pair of unequal tiles reads as hanging off to one side. Also note bg-1.jpg is still 500x280 and the new vignette makes the frame MORE visible, so the upscaling shows more than it used to; that needs a real photograph.

T-0293..T-0295 (share cards + SEO for every public URL) are in REVIEW, coupled to backend T-0217..T-0219 on the same work. DEPLOY ORDER MATTERS AND THE EDGE IS MANUAL. Ship the API first, then this web image, then hand-sync the Caddyfile: its @crawler matcher now lists /u/* /roster /roster/* /events /events/* /gallery /gallery/* /home, and a path listed there with no route under /api/seo/* returns a JSON 404, which an unfurler renders as a broken preview. deploy/README.md step 4 in the backend repo carries the exact verification loop.

Non-obvious decisions worth not relitigating. (1) `/` is deliberately NOT in the crawler matcher and `/home` is there instead - `/` is the one path a Cloudflare Cache Rule covers, Cloudflare honours Vary only for Accept-Encoding, so a UA-varying `/` would put the crawler document in the edge cache and serve it to humans. The sitemap lists /home for the same reason. (2) A profile with no banner declares twitter:card=summary ON PURPOSE: Discord inspects the real file and demotes a square avatar to a thumbnail whatever the tag says, so asking for the wide card and not getting it looks broken. (3) Titles are `<page> | <Regiment>` on BOTH surfaces now - the shells used an em dash, so every crawlable URL had two different titles. documentTitle() in the API's html/brand.ts and SeoService.apply() here are the same rule. (4) core/seo/seo-copy.ts is a contract with the backend: changing a function there without its twin in the API's SeoService desyncs the two surfaces for as long as the versions are split. (5) RegimentService.getProfile() is cached for the tab now, because five components need the live regiment name for their description.

Verification state: 794 frontend tests green, ng lint clean, prettier clean; 1270 backend tests green, eslint + prettier clean. The routing was exercised for real against a throwaway Caddy on :8899 in front of the dev stack - every path returns the shell to a Discordbot UA and <app-root> to a browser UA, and the honest 404s (/u/@nobody, a missing event) still come through. All seven URLs were diffed live in the browser: title and description MATCH the shell on every one. NOT done: no video gallery item exists in the dev DB, so the og:video path is covered by unit tests only and has never been pasted into a real Discord channel.

Still true from T-0289..T-0292: those remain in review on feat/member-bio-and-socials, and the browser passes in their testPlans are still pending.

tasks.title: Fix production CSS broken by CSP-blocked critical-CSS deferral
tasks.summary: The first production deploy rendered half-styled. Angular's inlineCritical (beasties, on by default under optimization:true) emits the deferred-stylesheet pattern - the main sheet is linked at media="print" and an inline onload="this.media='all'" handler promotes it once loaded. The edge serves script-src 'self', so the browser blocks that inline event handler, the sheet stays scoped to print and is never applied to screen; only the inlined critical subset renders. The asset itself was always fine (200 text/css). Inline handlers cannot be hash-whitelisted without 'unsafe-hashes', so the fix is in the build, not the CSP: pin optimization.styles.inlineCritical:false for production so a plain render-blocking <link> is emitted. Costs ~18kB gzipped of blocking CSS. scripts/fonts/styles.minify stay true, so Google Fonts CSS is still inlined (CSP-safe via style-src 'unsafe-inline'). Invisible outside production: the development configuration sets optimization:false and ng serve sends no CSP header. Documented as a do-not-re-enable warning in CLAUDE.md.

testPlan.desc: Prod build emits <link rel="stylesheet"> with no onload and no media="print"
No inline event handlers remain anywhere in the emitted index.html
Google Fonts @font-face CSS is still inlined into a <style> block
Bundle hashes unchanged and initial bundle stays within the 540kB warning budget
186/186 unit tests pass
After deploy: lordsofholdfast.com/home renders fully styled with no CSP error for the stylesheet

regressionRisk.desc: Changes the production optimization block from the implicit boolean true to an object. Any sub-flag omitted from the object falls back to its schema default rather than to true, so a future edit that drops scripts/fonts/styles.minify would silently de-optimise the bundle. The budget check in CI is the backstop - initial total is currently 122.36kB transfer against a 540kB raw warning threshold, so a de-optimised build would not necessarily trip it.

skippedByClaude: Did not touch the backend Caddyfile CSP - the Cloudflare Insights beacon being blocked is cosmetic (analytics do not report; nothing user-facing breaks) and the choice between disabling Web Analytics vs widening script-src to a third-party origin is the user's. tasks.title: Render event times in the viewer local timezone
tasks.summary: Event times are printed in the event author timezone ("2026-07-22 - 20:18 to 02:00 UTC"), so a member in EDT has to convert by hand. questions.q: Should the original authored timezone still be shown as secondary context (e.g. "16:18 - 22:00 (20:18 UTC)"), or is the local time alone enough?
questions.answer: Show the VIEWER's zone label (e.g. 'EDT'), not the authored one. Once the time is converted, printing the authored IANA zone beside it is actively misleading - that combination was the original bug. `viewerZoneLabel(iso)` resolves the abbreviation per instant, so a summer and a winter event each label correctly.

tasks.title: Stop the profile name rendering on top of the banner on mobile
tasks.summary: On a phone the display name and the Edit button rendered INSIDE the banner instead of below it. The desktop rule pulls the whole .profile-header up 40-48px and relies on `align-items: flex-end` to push the text back down — which only holds while .profile-header-info is SHORTER than the 132px avatar. At phone widths the rigid action buttons squeeze that column to ~106px, the 24px serif name wraps to two lines, the info block becomes the tallest flex item (~147px), and bottom-aligning the tallest item is a no-op: its top edge IS the container's, i.e. 40px inside the banner. Actions drop to their own full-width row, the shape the mobile design reference specifies, which also frees the width that made the name wrap.

tasks.title: Derive-from-Discord button, and a confirmation for every admin action
tasks.summary: Two halves of the same complaint: an admin presses something in the member admin modal and cannot tell what happened. (1) A new Discord section offers "Derive data from Discord" with the hint "It will derive rank and medals already assigned on Discord side.", calling the new POST /members/:id/derive-from-discord (backend T-0204). It is the one action whose effect the caller cannot predict, so the server's own summary sentence is shown twice - as a toast AND left in the dialog, where the list of medals that came across can be re-read after the toast has gone. A run that found nothing is reported in the neutral (info) tone, not as an achievement. (2) EVERY admin action now raises a success toast. Failures have raised one since T-0246; successes raised nothing at all, and these dialogs sit over a page the change is not visible on - a role change swaps a value in a select that already showed it, a medal removal takes away a chip nobody was looking at, so a completed action and a click that silently did nothing looked identical. Each message is built from the member the SERVER returned rather than from the local form state, so it reports what landed; the award/remove messages read their medal title BEFORE the request, because the select is cleared and the chip is gone by the time it resolves. The existing toast component was already the dark elevated-ink card T-0270 made it, so no new surface was needed.

tasks.title: Explain the partial lockout when only the moderation half is withheld
tasks.summary: Companion to backend T-0211, which stopped subjecting rank and medal writes to the role hierarchy: an edit_ranks_medals holder may now decorate a peer, a senior, the regiment owner and their OWN record, while role/suspend/ban keep the full rule. No gate in this repo changed - every getter is already `capability && !!actions?.<flag>` and parsePermittedActions copies the block key-for-key, so the widened flags flow straight through. What changed is that a permittedActions block can now MIX true and false for one target, which produced a UI state the modal had no words for: a Moderator opening an Admin sees Rank, Medals and Derive working while Role, Suspend and Ban are simply absent. The only explanation of a hierarchy lockout lived in the all-or-nothing `!hasAnyPermittedAction` branch, which no longer fires for exactly the two cases it was written for. Adds moderationAvailable + moderationLockedOut and a second notice placed in the gap the missing sections leave, and narrows every sentence derived from standsLevelOrAbove from 'this record can only be managed by someone who outranks them' to the role/suspension/ban half - the old wording is now visibly untrue with the rank control on screen. The notice is suppressed for a caller who never held manage_roles: telling them a rule was applied that they were not subject to is noise. Also unpins the section divider from the Ban section (`:last-of-type`), because a rank/medal-only admin never renders Suspend or Ban and was left with a dangling rule. The owner then widened it again mid-review to include the caller's own record, which made two previously-unreachable states real: the roster `···` appears on your own row, and T-0246's disabled-and-explained Suspend/Ban treatment - written defensively for a dialog that never opened on self - is now the thing explaining the two dead controls beside a live rank picker.

tasks.title: Show medals in cabinet order, and centre the Honours panel on the medal's own description
tasks.summary: Three fixes to how a member's decorations read. (1) ORDER: nothing here changes — the roster, the profile panel and the dashboard strip already render `medalAwards` verbatim, so the backend's precedence sort (lords-dashboard-backend T-0212) corrects all three plus the admin dialog chips for free. `precedence` is deliberately kept off the award shape so no client sort can creep back in; a spec pins that the mapper preserves the API's order, repeats included. (2) DESCRIPTION: `MemberMedalAward` gains `description` — the catalogue text /admin/ranks edits — and the Honours & Decorations panel now shows it instead of `award.detail`. `detail` was the per-award citation, which on the live roster is the same sentence on every medal ('Derived from their existing Discord roles'); a viewer wants to know what the medal TAKES. The field had to be threaded through all three hops — ApiMemberMedal, MemberMedalAward, and the `mapMedalAward` whitelist copy, which drops unknown wire fields with no type error. (3) LAYOUT: `.medal-item` was `align-items: flex-start`, pinning a ~48px text block to the top of a 64px hf-medal tile; it is now `center`, with `.medal-info` given its own column box so title and description centre as one block. Measured, not asserted from the stylesheet: the spec fails at a 16.3px offset under the old rule and passes at 0.00px under the new one.

tasks.title: Give SeoService a card image, video tags and per-page canonicals
tasks.summary: SeoTags gained SeoImage/SeoVideo, og:locale, og:image:secure_url/width/height/alt, the og:video set, rel=prev/next and an explicit indexable robots directive with max-image-preview:large. apply() previously REMOVED og:image whenever a page passed none, which deleted index.html's static default the moment Angular booted - so the landing page, the roster, the calendar and the gallery index all unfurled with no picture at all. There is now a shipped-banner fallback matching the API's DEFAULT_CARD_IMAGE, and twitter:card is chosen three ways (player / summary_large_image / summary) instead of two, because Discord demotes a square image to a thumbnail whatever the tag claims.

testPlan.desc: seo: a page with no image of its own still emits og:image (the shipped banner), not none
seo: a square avatar asks for twitter:card=summary; a banner asks for summary_large_image
seo: rel=prev/next are added and REMOVED again across a navigation
BROWSER: every public route's live tags match /api/seo/<path> byte for byte

regressionRisk.desc: RegimentService.getProfile() is now shareReplay(1) with refCount:false, so the public regiment projection is cached for the lifetime of the tab. Five components depend on it for their meta description. An officer renaming the regiment will not see the new name in a share card until a reload; the admin surface reads /settings, which is uncached.

tasks.title: Make every public page's card image and copy match the crawler shell
tasks.summary: landing, roster, events, event detail, gallery and gallery detail all now pass a card image and build their description from the LIVE regiment name via core/seo/seo-copy.ts, whose functions are one-to-one with the API's SeoService. Four of them hardcoded 'Lords Regiment' while the shell read the editable field. The roster canonicalised every page to /roster, so page 2 onwards asked Google to drop every profile only linked from there; it now carries a per-page canonical plus rel=prev/next. gallery-page never re-applied after its fetch and emitted no structured data at all.

testPlan.desc: roster: page 2 canonicalises to itself and carries rel=prev
gallery: the index re-applies after load with the newest still as its card and an ImageGallery payload
event detail: the no-description fallback names the date in the EVENT's timezone, not the reader's
profile: the banner is the card when set, the avatar (declared square) otherwise
BROWSER: all seven shareable URLs match the shell's title and description exactly

skippedByClaude: Left the SPA's theme-color at --ink-900 (#0b0e14) rather than the brass the shells send Discord: that meta tags the MOBILE BROWSER CHROME to match the page background, and no unfurler ever reads the SPA's copy.

tasks.title: Allow the unfurlers explicitly in robots.txt, and stop /me competing with /u/@handle
tasks.summary: Whether Discordbot honours robots.txt is genuinely contested - its own issue tracker carries reports of a restrictive robots.txt suppressing embeds. The wildcard group already allowed everything, so the four named groups change nothing today; they exist so a future Disallow added for human reasons cannot silently take every link preview down with it. /me is also disallowed now: it is authGuard'd and resolves to the caller's own indexable /u/@handle, so the two were competing for one page.

testPlan.desc: robots: the file still parses and still points at the generated sitemap

tasks.title: Rebuild the landing hero around one command and a stats plinth
tasks.summary: The hero carried three equal btn-lg buttons, two of which (Orders, Roster) are already in the public nav two rows above, so its one decisive moment was spent on links the visitor already had. Down to one CTA. The flat top-to-bottom scrim becomes a radial vignette that stays dark behind the type and lets the photograph read at the frame. The two figures KEEP the old stat-tile treatment (big brass serif value over an uppercase label) but move BELOW the command rather than between it and the copy it acts on, under a contained hairline rule, as equal columns - '11 / 2023' is three times the width of '2', so packing the pair around the centre left the block visibly hanging to one side. The roll is now a link to /roster, with a persistent arrow cue rather than a hover-only one. Fixed while in there: .hero-crest's ring was NEVER DRAWN - rgba(var(--brass-300), .3) cannot resolve (the token is a hex, not an r,g,b triple), which invalidated the whole border shorthand and left border-style:none. Both scrim layers stay parameterised on --hero-scrim so the admin's overlay density (T-0238) still works.

testPlan.desc: 800 unit tests green, ng lint + contrast guard clean, prettier clean, production build succeeds
browser: /home at 1180px and 1920px against the live dev stack - crest ring drawn, single CTA, vignette lets the banner read at the edges, both stat columns balanced under the rule
browser: /home at 390px - crest 76px, full-bleed CTA, stat columns still balanced and labels still on one line
browser: the members figure resolves to href=/roster in the real DOM (confirmed via --dump-dom) - still needs a real click-through to confirm SPA nav rather than a full reload
browser: admin overlay density 0 and 100 on the new radial vignette - 0 really is a bare photograph and 100 does not black out the type
browser: a regiment with statistics visibility OFF - the hero ends at the CTA with no orphaned divider rule

regressionRisk.desc: landing.component.spec.ts's RegimentService mock now reads a swappable stats$ instead of a hardcoded of(null). The default is still of(null), so every pre-existing spec sees exactly the behaviour it saw before, but a future spec that forgets to reset it would leak the figures into an unrelated assertion.
formatEstablished() now returns 'MM / YYYY' rather than 'MM/YYYY'. Only the hero consumes it today; any future reader that parses the string rather than printing it would break on the spaces.

skippedByClaude: Did NOT replace src/assets/images/bg-1.jpg. The design note flags it as 500x280, so it upscales roughly 3x on a desktop hero - the new vignette makes the edges MORE visible, not less, so this matters more than it did. Needs a real photograph, not a code change.
Did NOT touch the login hero, which still uses the old flat scrim - the import covered the homepage hero only, and the two now differ.

The design's own concept moved the figures onto a hairline plinth on the hero's bottom edge; that was built and then reverted to the stat-tile treatment at the user's request. Only the placement (below the command, not between it and the copy) survives from the concept.
